Container.Name: GitHub-Runner
Container.Overview:
Self-hosted GitHub Actions runners for several repositories in one container.
Why this template exists: a personal GitHub account can attach a self-hosted runner to a single repository only. Sharing one runner across repositories needs an organization. The usual runner templates therefore need one container per repository. This one starts a runner for every repository you list and keeps them all in one container.
• List your repositories as owner/name, separated by spaces or commas. Each one gets its own runner named GitHub-Runner. • Stopping the container removes every runner from GitHub again, so your repositories never fill up with offline leftovers. • A repository the token cannot reach is reported in the log and tried again every five minutes. The others keep running. • Map the Docker socket and your jobs can build images and start containers.
You need a personal access token that may manage runners in every listed repository: a fine-grained token with Administration: Read and write on those repositories, or a classic token with the repo scope.
Everything is managed in the web interface on port 8080: add and remove repositories, watch the runners and their jobs, replace the token and set an optional password. The fields below only fill the settings on the first start. A new token here replaces the saved one at the next start, and repositories new in the list are added.
In your workflows, use runs-on: self-hosted.
A self-hosted runner runs whatever the workflow tells it to. Use it for your own repositories, not for public ones where strangers can open pull requests.
Built on myoung34/github-runner. Not affiliated with GitHub.

Container.Requires: A GitHub personal access token with administration rights on every repository you add. You can paste it here or later in the web interface.

Config.Name: Web Interface
Config.Description: The port of the web interface.

Config.Name: Config
Config.Description: Settings, repositories and the job history of the last two days. Back it up to keep them.

Config.Name: Access Token
Config.Description: Personal access token that may manage runners in your repositories. Fine-grained: Administration: Read and write on those repositories. Classic: the repo scope. Optional here, you can also paste it in the web interface. A new value replaces the saved token at the next start.

Config.Name: Repositories
Config.Description: Repositories that get a runner, as owner/name, separated by spaces or commas. For example: you/website you/backend. Optional, you can add them in the web interface. New entries are added at the next start, one taken out keeps its runner until you remove it in the web interface.

Config.Name: Owner
Config.Description: Owner for repositories written without one, so Repositories can be just website backend.

Config.Name: Docker Socket
Config.Description: Lets your jobs build images and start containers on this server. Remove it if your workflows do not use Docker. Anything with the socket can control every container here, so only list repositories you trust.

Config.Name: Runner Name
Config.Description: Name of the runner in every repository, as shown under Settings, Actions, Runners.

Config.Name: Labels
Config.Description: Extra labels for the runners, comma-separated. Workflows pick a runner by its labels in runs-on.

Config.Name: No Default Labels
Config.Description: true drops the labels GitHub adds by itself (self-hosted, Linux, X64), so only jobs that ask for your own labels run here.

Config.Name: Run As Root
Config.Description: false runs the runners as the unprivileged runner user instead of root.

Config.Name: Remove On Stop
Config.Description: Removes the runners from GitHub when the container stops and registers them again on start. false keeps them listed as offline while stopped.

Config.Name: Retry Seconds
Config.Description: How long to wait before trying again a repository that could not be registered.

Config.Name: Dashboard Group
Config.Description: The section dashboards that read container labels list GitHub-Runner under.

Config.Name: Dashboard Name
Config.Description: The name dashboards that read container labels show.

Config.Name: Dashboard Icon
Config.Description: The logo dashboards that read container labels show.

Config.Name: Dashboard Description
Config.Default: GitHub Actions runners for several repositories
Config.Description: The short line dashboards that read container labels show under the name.

Container.Config: GitHub Actions runners for several repositories

Config.Name: Alt Dashboard Name
Config.Description: The same name under the glance.* keys, which other dashboards read.

Config.Name: Alt Dashboard Icon
Config.Description: The same logo under the glance.* keys.

Config.Name: Alt Dashboard Description
Config.Default: GitHub Actions runners for several repositories
Config.Description: The same short line under the glance.* keys.
